facts.statement: Prestosuchus is an extinct genus of pseudosuchian belonging to the group Loricata that lived in Brazil during the Middle Triassic.
facts.quote: Prestosuchus (meaning "Prestes' crocodile") is an extinct genus of pseudosuchian in the group Loricata, from the Middle Triassic of Brazil.

facts.statement: The fossil range of Prestosuchus is the Middle Triassic, specifically the Ladinian stage.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle Triassic (Ladinian),

facts.statement: The holotype of Prestosuchus chiniquensis was discovered by Wilhelm Rau alongside the holotype of Rauisuchus tiradentes.
facts.quote: The holotype of Prestosuchus chiniquensis was discovered by Wilhelm Rau alongside the holotype of Rauisuchus tiradentes.

facts.statement: The holotypes were found in 1928 or 1929 within the Santa Maria Formation at the Paleontological Site Chiniquá near São Pedro do Sul, Brazil.
facts.quote: Both were found in 1928 or 1929 within the Santa Maria Formation at Paleontological Site Chiniquá, near the city of São Pedro do Sul in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene named the genus Prestosuchus in 1938 to honor the Brazilian paleontologist Vicentino Prestes de Almeida.
facts.quote: Von Huene named the genus Prestosuchus in 1938 in honor of Brazilian paleontologist Vicentino Prestes de Almeida.

facts.statement: The Chiniquá fossil site is now part of the Paleorrota geopark.
facts.quote: The Chiniquá site is now part of the geopark of Paleorrota.

facts.statement: A specific partial skeleton specimen was designated as the lectotype of Prestosuchus chiniquensis in 1972.
facts.quote: In 1972, this specimen was designated as the lectotype of Prestosuchus chiniquensis.

facts.statement: The lectotype and paralectotype specimens of Prestosuchus chiniquensis are stored at the Bavarian State Collection for Palaeontology and Geology in Munich, Germany.
facts.quote: The lectotype and paralectotype are stored at the Bavarian State Collection for Palaeontology and Geology (Bayerische Staatsammlung für Paläontologie und Geologie, BSPG) institute of the Bavarian Natural History Collections (Staatliche Naturwissenschaftliche Sammlungen Bayerns, or SNSB) in Munich, Germany.

facts.statement: The only Prestosuchus fossil stored outside Brazil and Germany is a fragmentary specimen held at Harvard's Museum of Comparative Zoology in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
facts.quote: The only Prestosuchus fossil stored outside of Brazil or Germany is MCZ 4167, an obscure and fragmentary specimen found at "Posto de Gasolina" and held at Harvard's Museum of Comparative Zoology in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

facts.statement: Prestosuchus has historically been classified as a rauisuchian and as the defining member of the family Prestosuchidae.
facts.quote: Alongside relatives such as Saurosuchus and Postosuchus, Prestosuchus has historically been referred to as a "rauisuchian", as well as the defining member of the family Prestosuchidae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the groups Rauisuchia and Prestosuchidae are valid, as Rauisuchia is considered paraphyletic and Prestosuchidae is polyphyletic in its widest form.
facts.quote: The validity of both of these groups is questionable. "Rauisuchia" is now considered a paraphyletic group of large carnivorous pseudosuchians ancestral to crocodylomorphs. Prestosuchidae is polyphyletic in its widest form, though it may retain some utility in a narrower sense centered on Prestosuchus.

facts.statement: There is an ongoing debate regarding the exact number of species contained within the genus Prestosuchus.
facts.quote: There has been some debate over exactly how many species are contained within Prestosuchus.

facts.statement: Some researchers have suggested that Procerosuchus celer and Prestosuchus loricatus are junior synonyms of Prestosuchus chiniquensis.
facts.quote: Some authors have considered Procerosuchus celer or Prestosuchus loricatus to be junior synonyms of Prestosuchus chiniquensis.

facts.statement: All undisputed fossils of Prestosuchus come from the lower Santa Maria Formation in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
facts.quote: All undisputed Prestosuchus fossils are from the lower Santa Maria Formation (Dinodontosaurus assemblage zone) of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.

facts.statement: Researchers Kischlat and Barberena (1999) proposed that certain Prestosuchus fossils, including the paralectotype of P. chiniquensis and the Porto Alegre specimen, should be classified as a new genus and species.
facts.quote: A brief abstract by Kischlat & Barberena (1999) claimed that several Prestosuchus specimens, including the paralectotype of P. chiniquensis and the giant "Porto Alegre specimen" (i.e. UFRGS-PV-0156-T), actually deserve a new genus and species.

facts.statement: Kischlat (2000) proposed the name "Karamuru vorax" for specific fossils previously referred to Prestosuchus, based on a 1999 abstract.
facts.quote: Kischlat (2000) later used the name "Karamuru vorax" in reference to these fossils, citing the 1999 abstract as the name's origin.

facts.statement: The names "Karamuru vorax" and "Abaporu" are considered invalid scientific names because they were not formally published according to ICZN standards.
facts.quote: These informal treatments do not pass ICZN standards for new scientific names, so "Karamuru vorax" and "Abaporu" are considered invalid nomina nuda by the wider community.

facts.statement: Kischlat (2023) suggested renaming the species Prestosuchus chiniquensis to the new genus Huenesuchus.
facts.quote: Later, Kischlat (2023) proposed that Prestosuchus chiniquensis should receive a new genus name, Huenesuchus.

facts.statement: Other paleontologists disagreed with Kischlat's arguments regarding the renaming of Prestosuchus chiniquensis.
facts.quote: Other paleontologists immediately disagreed with Kischlat's arguments in informal contexts.

facts.statement: Desojo and Rauhut (2008) argued that Procerosuchus celer is a junior synonym of Prestosuchus chiniquensis.
facts.quote: A 2008 abstract by Desojo & Rauhut argued that Procerosuchus celer was a junior synonym of Prestosuchus chiniquensis.

facts.statement: Later studies by the same authors disagree with their earlier finding that Procerosuchus celer is a junior synonym of Prestosuchus chiniquensis.
facts.quote: Later studies, many of which include the same authors, disagree with this preliminary finding.

facts.statement: Desojo and colleagues (2020) argued that "Prestosuchus" loricatus deserves its own genus and proposed a new name.
facts.quote: Desojo et al. (2020) indicated that "Prestosuchus" loricatus deserved its own genus, and that a new name was forthcoming.

facts.statement: Desojo and colleagues (2020) argued that Stagonosuchus nyassicus should be classified as the second valid species of Prestosuchus, named Prestosuchus nyassicus.
facts.quote: Desojo et al. (2020) argued that it should be lumped into Prestosuchus as a second valid species, Prestosuchus nyassicus.

facts.statement: Smith and colleagues (2024) suggested that Stagonosuchus belongs within Poposauroidea rather than Loricata.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis by Smith et al. (2024) recovered Stagonosuchus outside Loricata and suggested that it could be included within Poposauroidea instead.

facts.statement: Prestosuchus possessed a deep skull and serrated teeth similar to its relatives.
facts.quote: Like its relatives, Prestosuchus had a deep skull and serrated teeth.

facts.statement: Prestosuchus lived during the Middle Triassic in the region that is now Brazil.
facts.quote: Prestosuchus lived during the Middle Triassic in what is now Brazil.

facts.statement: Prestosuchus likely walked on four legs with an upright semi-erect stance, having limb bones positioned below the hips, unlike modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Prestosuchus probably walked on four legs like crocodilians, but unlike crocodilians, it had an upright semi-erect stance with limb bones placed below the hips.

facts.statement: The premaxilla of Prestosuchus has a tall, boxy main body containing four teeth.
facts.quote: The premaxilla has a tall and boxy main body with four teeth.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Prestosuchus is deep and roughly textured, featuring a low triangular antorbital fenestra and 11 to 13 large teeth.
facts.quote: The maxilla is deep and roughly textured, with a low, triangular antorbital fenestra and 11-13 large teeth.

facts.statement: Many Prestosuchus specimens appear to have a thin convex ridge, or "roman nose," along the midline of the nasals, similar to Luperosuchus and Batrachotomus.
facts.quote: Many specimens seemingly possessed a thin convex ridge ("roman nose") running along the midline of the elongated and narrow nasals, similar to Luperosuchus and Batrachotomus.

facts.statement: The orbit of Prestosuchus has an overall "keyhole" shape, with a smoother, wider upper border and a narrow, pointed lower half.
facts.quote: The orbit has an overall "keyhole" shape like many other loricatans, with its upper half having a smoother and wider border and its lower half being narrow and pointed.

facts.statement: The dentary bone of the lower jaw in Prestosuchus contains 14 teeth.
facts.quote: There are 14 teeth in the dentary, the main tooth-bearing bone of the lower jaw.

facts.statement: The splenial bone in Prestosuchus is unusually elongated, extending forward as far as the second tooth in the jaw.
facts.quote: The splenial, which lies on the inner surface of the dentary, is unusually elongated in Prestosuchus and extends as far forward as the second tooth in the jaw.

facts.statement: The neck vertebrae of Prestosuchus are tall and feature large ventral depressions that create a keel on their lower edge.
facts.quote: Cervical (neck) vertebrae are notably tall and their sides are excavated by large ventral depressions, which generates a keel on their lower edge.

facts.statement: Prestosuchus had two-headed dorsal ribs similar to those of Batrachotomus and a dense gastral basket.
facts.quote: Prestosuchus also possessed two-headed dorsal ribs which were similar in shape to those of Batrachotomus, as well as a dense gastral basket.

facts.statement: Prestosuchus possessed two sacral vertebrae, though it is unclear if they were fused.
facts.quote: There are two sacral vertebrae, and it is unclear whether they are fused to each other.

facts.statement: Individual osteoderms in Prestosuchus were wide, roughly heart-shaped, and multiple osteoderms were located above each vertebra.
facts.quote: Individual osteoderms were wide, roughly heart-shaped, and more than one osteoderm per row was present above each vertebra.

facts.statement: In Prestosuchus, the scapula and coracoid are strongly connected but not fused.
facts.quote: The scapula and coracoid are strongly connected to each other but not fused.

facts.statement: The coracoid bone in Prestosuchus is low and approximately twice as long as it is high.
facts.quote: The coracoid is low, about twice as long as it is high.

facts.statement: The hand anatomy of Prestosuchus is mostly unknown, with only a single metacarpal discovered that is widest near the wrist.
facts.quote: The hand is a mostly unknown anatomical area in Prestosuchus; only a single metacarpal has been discovered and it is widest towards the wrist.

facts.statement: The ilium of Prestosuchus features a deep bony acetabulum covered by a horizontal supraacetabular crest.
facts.quote: The ilium has a deep bony acetabulum roofed by a horizontal supraacetabular crest.

facts.statement: The pubis in Prestosuchus is straight and contributes only slightly to the acetabulum above the obturator foramen.
facts.quote: The pubis is straight, with a small contribution to the acetabulum above the obturator foramen.

facts.statement: The femur of Prestosuchus is very robust and lacks a clear neck connecting the shaft to the head.
facts.quote: The femur is very robust, without a clear neck leading from the shaft of the bone to the head.

facts.statement: Some researchers consider the unique notch at the scapula-coracoid suture an autapomorphy of Prestosuchus, as it has not been reported in other loricatans.
facts.quote: This notch has not been reported in any other loricatan and some have considered it an autapomorphy (unique distinguishing feature) of Prestosuchus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the horizontal ridge on the coracoid is a unique feature of P. chiniquensis, as it has also been found in Procerosuchus and Batrachotomus.
facts.quote: The horizontal ridge may be an autapomorphy of P. chiniquensis, yet it has also been reported in Procerosuchus and Batrachotomus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether "P." loricatus belongs to Prestosuchus, as it lacks several pelvic autapomorphies found in P. chiniquensis and P. nyassicus, suggesting it may be a different genus.
facts.quote: Several autapomorphies of Prestosuchus relate to the pelvis (hip). These traits are present in P. chiniquensis and P. nyassicus (Stagonosuchus), but notably absent in "P." loricatus, which is likely a different genus.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the leg musculature of Prestosuchus represents a primitive condition for archosaurs rather than a derived one.
facts.quote: indicating that the musculature of Prestosuchus better represents a basal ("primitive") condition for archosaurs than it does a derived condition for crocodile-line or pseudosuchian archosaurs.

facts.statement: Prestosuchus was likely an apex predator in its habitat.
facts.quote: It was likely an apex predator of its habitat.

facts.statement: A notable complete skeleton with a well-preserved hind limb was discovered in 2010 in Dona Francisca, Rio Grande do Sul, by a team from the Universidade Luterana do Brasil.
